itineraries.title: Block Party Saturday — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A cool-ish morning at the art museum, then the two biggest free street parties in the city, four miles apart
itineraries.drive_time: About 25 minutes of driving all day. NCMA to Hillsborough Street is 10 minutes; Hillsborough Street to Dix Park is another 10. Park once downtown if you can and use the greenway or a scooter between the last two.

weather.summary: Chance of rain showers and thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$40 per person. Every event here is free; the money goes on food and a parking deck.
itineraries.overview: 87°F with scattered afternoon storms in the forecast, so this route front-loads the outdoor exertion and treats the evening as the payoff. Packapalooza runs eight hours and 90,000 people show up; Kirby Derby is the opposite — a neighborhood soapbox race on a hill. Doing both means one short hop mid-afternoon.

morning.title: NCMA Dance Gumbo: Dance Fitness with Jordan Farrell
morning.location: Museum Park, North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
morning.notes: 45 minutes outdoors before the heat lands. If you'd rather watch than move, the park's trails and the Ellsworth Kelly wall are right there.

morning.title: In Motion. In Time. — a choreographic response in the galleries
morning.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
morning.notes: Short, indoors, air-conditioned. A good excuse to stay at NCMA through the hottest part of the late morning.

afternoon.title: Packapalooza 2026
afternoon.location: Hillsborough Street at Founders Drive, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: 350+ vendor booths and multiple music stages down a closed Hillsborough Street. Go in through the west end near Gorman if you're driving; the Dan Allen deck is the least painful parking.

afternoon.title: Kirby Derby
afternoon.location: Harvey Hill, Dix Park, 1030 Richardson Dr, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Ten minutes south. Wacky downhill soapbox racing, a kids' pinebox competition, a parade and live music. Costumes encouraged, shade is scarce — pick a spot on the tree line.

evening.title: Back to Packapalooza for the music and fireworks
evening.notes: The festival runs to 10 PM and closes with fireworks at the Belltower. The evening stages are the reason to come back rather than stay at Dix.

food.vegan_dish: Ask for the tofu scramble or an avocado toast built without butter — the counter will tell you what's vegan that morning
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit or a veggie omelette
food.notes: 8 W Peace St, on the way from downtown to NCMA. Small, quick, opens early on a Saturday.

food.vegan_dish: Several trucks on Hillsborough Street run plant-based menus; ask before you queue — the lineup changes yearly
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, arepas, fries and shaved ice are reliable on the street
food.notes: Cash is faster than card when the lines are long. Eat before 3 PM; the food rows jam after the afternoon stages start.

food.vegan_dish: The stalls rotate, but at least one counter usually plates a fully plant-based bowl — ask each vendor directly
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza or a vegetable-heavy plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 500 E Davie St. Air conditioning, multiple kitchens, no reservation needed. A ten-minute drive from Dix Park before you head back to Hillsborough Street.

alternatives.good_weather: Walk the whole street end to end, then camp near the Belltower for the fireworks.
alternatives.rain: Scattered storms are in the forecast. The NC Museum of Natural Sciences downtown is free and open, and the 2 PM Museum Untold Tour ($25) is a solid indoor pivot; the ComedyWorx 4 PM matinee on Hillsborough Street is a five-minute walk from the festival footprint.

alternatives.leg: Kirby Derby (3:30 PM, Harvey Hill, no shelter)
alternatives.good_weather: Bring a blanket and sit on the hill above the finish line.
alternatives.rain: Dix Park has almost no cover on Harvey Hill. Fall back to Marbles Kids Museum downtown (Kick-off to Kindergarten runs all day, from $9) or A Night of Poe at Lincoln Theatre at 2 PM ($55).

practical_notes: 87°F with afternoon storms possible. Both afternoon events are fully exposed — carry water and check radar before you commit to the Dix Park leg.
Packapalooza closes Hillsborough Street from roughly Gorman to Oberlin; the Dan Allen and Coliseum decks are your best bets, and street parking near the festival is gone by noon.
Dix Park's lots fill for Kirby Derby. The Umstead Drive entrance is usually the last to clog.
NCMA's People's Collection and the Museum Park are free; only some programs are ticketed.
The fireworks are at the Belltower around 10 PM — if you leave right after, expect twenty minutes of pedestrian traffic before you can move a car.

itineraries.title: Fiftieth Lazy Daze — Cary and Morrisville
itineraries.theme: A morning market in Morrisville, 250 artists on the Cary Town Hall campus, and a free Delta Rae show to close it
itineraries.drive_time: Under 20 minutes of driving. Morrisville to downtown Cary is 12 minutes; Town Hall campus to Downtown Cary Park is a four-minute walk, so you park once and stay parked.

weather.summary: Chance of rain showers and thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $0–$50 per person. The market, the festival and the concert are all free; you're paying for craft, lunch and whatever the beer garden costs.
itineraries.overview: This is the 50th Lazy Daze, which means four entertainment stages, 25+ food vendors, a beer garden and a new Kid Collectors Market on top of the usual juried crafts. Downtown Cary is walkable and mostly shaded, which matters at 87°F. Stay through 7:30 and Delta Rae plays the park for free.

morning.title: Western Wake Farmers Market
morning.notes: This Saturday adds the Great Southeast Pollinator Census, a heartfulness meditation and an Indian cooking demo. No musician booked this week. Closes at noon, so come first.

morning.title: 50th Annual Lazy Daze Arts and Crafts Festival
morning.location: Cary Town Hall Campus, 316 N Academy St, Cary
morning.notes: Get there before the 11 AM crush. The artist rows are the quietest early, and the shade on the Academy Street side is the best on the campus.

afternoon.title: Lazy Daze, second half — stages, beer garden, Kid Collectors Market
afternoon.location: Cary Town Hall Campus, 316 N Academy St, Cary
afternoon.notes: Four stages run all afternoon. The Kid Collectors Market lets kids buy small pieces from the same artists, which is a better souvenir than a funnel cake.

evening.title: CaryLIVE! Delta Rae
evening.location: Great Lawn Pavilion, Downtown Cary Park, 327 S Academy St, Cary
evening.notes: North Carolina's own Delta Rae, free, on the Great Lawn. Bring a blanket or a folding chair; food trucks and craft drinks are on site.

food.vegan_dish: Fruit, bakery items and prepared foods vary by week — ask each vendor; several bakers keep a vegan tray
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastries, kolaches and breakfast tacos from the prepared-food vendors
food.notes: Eat at the market rather than sitting down somewhere. It's faster and it's the point of coming.

food.vegan_dish: 25+ vendors; look for the falafel, arepa and fresh-fruit stands, and ask about butter and cheese before ordering
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, mac and cheese, kettle corn and lemonade are festival constants
food.notes: The beer garden and Lazy Lounge are where the seating and shade are. Lines peak 12–2.

food.place: Downtown Cary Park food trucks / Academy Street restaurants
food.vegan_dish: Academy Street has several kitchens that will build a plant-based plate on request; the park's trucks change weekly, so ask
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza, pasta or a vegetable plate from the Academy Street strip
food.notes: Eat around 6 so you have a spot on the Great Lawn before the 7:30 set. The park's own trucks are the shortest walk.

alternatives.leg: Lazy Daze (9 AM–5 PM, outdoors on the Town Hall campus)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the full artist loop twice; the light on the Academy Street rows is better late afternoon.
alternatives.rain: The festival runs rain or shine but the crowd thins fast. Downtown Cary's indoor shops and the Cary Arts Center are a block away, and the festival repeats Sunday 9–5 if Saturday washes out.

alternatives.leg: CaryLIVE! Delta Rae (7:30 PM, Great Lawn, no roof)
alternatives.good_weather: Get on the lawn by 6:45 for a spot near the pavilion.
alternatives.rain: Free outdoor concerts here get cancelled for lightning, not drizzle. If it's called, the Squeeze / Adam Ant / Haircut 100 bill at Koka Booth is 10 minutes away on Sunday at 6 PM ($60+), or Night Nation Run takes over Koka Booth tonight from 5:30.

practical_notes: 87°F with a chance of storms. Downtown Cary has real shade; the Town Hall campus lawn does not.
Lazy Daze runs both Saturday and Sunday 9–5, so a rained-out Saturday isn't a lost weekend.
Park in the downtown Cary decks off Academy or Walnut — the festival and the park share the same walkable core, so one parking spot covers the whole day.
The Western Wake market closes at noon sharp; it is not worth reordering the day for.
Bring a chair for the concert. The Great Lawn fills from the pavilion outward.

itineraries.title: Tobacco, Vintage and Big Air — Durham
itineraries.theme: A working farm demonstration in the morning, a vintage market in the afternoon, and freestyle motocross inside the ballpark at night
itineraries.drive_time: About 30 minutes total. Duke Homestead is 10 minutes north of downtown; everything after lunch is inside the downtown loop and walkable from one deck.

weather.summary: Chance of rain showers and thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $15–$75 per person. The market, the harvest day and the vintage market are free; the BBQ plate is $12 and Nitro Circus is the real spend.
itineraries.overview: Durham's Saturday has an unusually good top end: Duke Homestead does its annual Brightleaf Harvest Day with live tobacco-looping demonstrations, and by night the Bulls' ballpark has a freestyle motocross ramp in it. In between, the Central Park pavilion runs a farmers market in the morning and a vintage market in the afternoon.

morning.title: Durham Farmers' Market
morning.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
morning.notes: Everything sold is grown or made within 70 miles. Under the pavilion, so the shade is guaranteed.

morning.title: Brightleaf Harvest Day at Duke Homestead
morning.location: Duke Homestead State Historic Site, 2828 Duke Homestead Rd, Durham
morning.notes: Staff and volunteers demonstrate tobacco looping and field harvesting — a nearly lost craft — on the farm where Durham's tobacco industry started. You can try it yourself.

afternoon.title: For the Girls Vintage Market
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Y2K-leaning vintage clothing back at the pavilion, four hours after the farmers market clears out of the same space.

evening.title: Nitro Circus 2.0
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: FMX, BMX, skate and scooter athletes on a ramp course built inside the ballpark. Loud, and better from the lower bowl than the berm.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan doughnuts are made daily and the bagel sandwiches can be built without egg or cheese — ask which flavors are vegan that morning, it rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese on a house bagel
food.notes: 1002 9th St. Opens early, which is what you want before an 8 AM market and a 10 AM drive north.

food.vegan_dish: The fundraiser plate is pork-based; pack something, or eat at Guasaca on the way back (black-bean arepa or bowl with plantains and guasacaca, no cheese or crema)
food.vegetarian_dish: The plate's potatoes, green beans and hushpuppies can be ordered without the pork — ask at the tent
food.notes: $12 for pulled pork, potatoes, green beans and hushpuppies, and it funds the site. If that doesn't work for your table, eat downtown after.

food.vegan_dish: Work the stalls — at least one counter usually plates a fully vegan bowl or sandwich; ask each vendor since the lineup rotates
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza or a vegetable-forward plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 530 Foster St, a seven-minute walk from the DBAP. Multiple kitchens, no reservation, and you can eat and still make a 7 PM start.

alternatives.leg: Brightleaf Harvest Day (10 AM–2 PM, mostly in the field)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the field demonstration and the full circuit of historic buildings.
alternatives.rain: The interpreters move into the barns and the packhouse, so it survives a shower. If it's a washout, the Museum of Life and Science is eight minutes away, or the Nasher (free admission) is fifteen.

alternatives.good_weather: Nothing to plan around — get there for gates and watch the ramp setup.
alternatives.rain: Storms delay ramp shows more readily than baseball. The Mountain Goats with Mary Gauthier play DPAC at 8 PM, three minutes' walk away, and Golden Hour at Ponysaurus runs from 7 under partial cover.

practical_notes: 87°F with scattered storms. Duke Homestead's demonstration field is completely exposed; the historic buildings are the only shade.
Duke Homestead is free — the only charge is the $12 barbecue plate, and that's a site fundraiser.
The Central Park pavilion hosts both the morning farmers market and the afternoon vintage market, so the same parking works twice.
DBAP decks fill early for a non-baseball event. The Church Street deck is a five-minute walk and usually still has room at 6:15.
Historic Stagville also runs guided tours today at 11, 1 and 3 ($2) if you'd rather trade the vintage market for more history.

itineraries.title: Third Friday — Downtown Durham
itineraries.theme: Twenty-plus galleries open late, a food-truck market in the park, and the Scrap Exchange's 35th birthday taking over CCB Plaza
itineraries.drive_time: Nearly none. Park once downtown and walk the whole evening; the furthest leg — Golden Belt — is a 12-minute walk or a 4-minute drive east.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$60 per person. The art walk and the plaza party are free; you're paying for dinner and, if you want it, a DPAC ticket.
itineraries.overview: Third Friday is Durham's monthly gallery crawl, and this month it doubles as the Scrap Exchange's 35th anniversary party — cardboard art, a giant puppet by Jeghetto, live music from Emma Jane and DJ MARRS on CCB Plaza. Foodie Fare sets up 20+ food trucks in Durham Central Park at the same time, so dinner solves itself.

afternoon.title: Foodie Fare
afternoon.location: Durham Central Park, 501 Foster St, Durham
afternoon.notes: A third-Friday food and art market under the pavilion — 20+ food trucks, local makers and live music. Eat here before the galleries open at 6.

evening.title: Third Friday Durham Art Walk & Gallery Crawl
evening.location: Starts at CCB Plaza, 201 N Corcoran St, Durham
evening.notes: Start at the plaza for the Scrap Exchange's birthday takeover, then work outward: Durham Art Guild, Through This Lens, Future Hooman and the shops along Main.

evening.title: The Long Exhale — Opening Reception
evening.location: 5 Points Gallery, 109 E Chapel Hill St, Durham
evening.notes: A group-show opening a block from the plaza; two hours only, so hit it early in the crawl.

evening.title: Third Friday Art Walk at Golden Belt
evening.location: Golden Belt Arts, 800 Taylor St, Durham
evening.notes: Studio artists open their doors in the old mill alongside the Durham Art Guild gallery. The most substantial single stop of the night.

evening.title: Hasan Hates Ronny | Ronny Hates Hasan (optional late add)
evening.location: Durham Performing Arts Center, 123 Vivian St, Durham
evening.notes: The show starts at 7, so this is an either/or with the art walk, not an and. Pick it if you'd rather have a headline night than a wandering one.

food.vegan_dish: Oat- or almond-milk drinks are standard, and the pastry case usually carries at least one vegan bake — ask at the counter
food.vegetarian_dish: Any of the espresso drinks plus a pastry
food.notes: 420 W Geer St, walkable from Central Park. Useful if you're starting the day downtown rather than arriving at 5.

food.vegan_dish: Arepa or bowl with black beans, plantains, avocado and guasacaca sauce — built without cheese or crema
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese arepa with plantains and the full sauce bar
food.notes: Fast, cheap and built to order at the counter, so swaps are easy.

food.place: Foodie Fare trucks, Durham Central Park
food.vegan_dish: Twenty-plus trucks rotate monthly; there is normally at least one fully plant-based kitchen — walk the row before committing
food.vegetarian_dish: Arepas, pizza, noodles and dumplings are usually all present
food.notes: Eating here rather than at a restaurant keeps you on the crawl's schedule and inside the same three-block radius.

alternatives.leg: The art walk itself (6–9 PM, outdoors between indoor venues)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the full loop from CCB Plaza east to Golden Belt.
alternatives.rain: Thunderstorms are likely Friday. The galleries are all indoors — the only exposure is the walking between them and the CCB Plaza programming. Golden Belt alone is a whole evening under one roof if the weather closes in.

alternatives.good_weather: Eat at the picnic tables and stay for the live music.
alternatives.rain: The pavilion is roofed but open-sided. Durham Food Hall at 530 Foster St is a two-minute walk and fully indoors.

practical_notes: Showers and thunderstorms are likely Friday — this is the most rain-proof itinerary of the week because almost every stop is indoors.
Third Friday is free and needs no ticket; venues set their own closing times but most run 6–9.
Street parking downtown is free after 7 PM on weekdays; before that, the Corcoran and Church Street decks are the closest.
The Scrap Exchange takeover is at CCB Plaza (201 N Corcoran St), not at the Scrap Exchange's own Lakewood store.
The DPAC show and the art walk overlap. Treat them as alternatives unless you only want the last hour of the crawl.

itineraries.title: Food Trucks and a Saxophone Quartet — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A trolley tour of Dix Park, the biggest food-truck rodeo in the Triangle, and the last free concert of the city's summer series
itineraries.drive_time: About 15 minutes of driving all day. Dix Park to Fayetteville Street is 6 minutes, Fayetteville Street to Fletcher Park is 7. All three are inside the beltline.
itineraries.cost_range: $10–$45 per person. The tour, the rodeo entry and the concert are free; you're paying by the plate.
itineraries.overview: Mostly sunny and 90°F — the best-weather day of the week, and a Sunday built almost entirely out of free things. Fayetteville Street closes for the food-truck rodeo from noon to six, and Raleigh Parks closes out its summer concert series at Fletcher Park at six with the Carpe Diem Saxophone Quartet.

afternoon.title: Guided Trolley Tour of Dix Park
afternoon.location: Stone Houses Visitor Center, Dix Park, 1030 Richardson Dr, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Two hours, seated, with the history of the Dorothea Dix campus. The trolley is the coolest way to see the park on a 90°F afternoon.

afternoon.title: Raleigh Food Truck Rodeo
afternoon.notes: Shop Local Raleigh closes Fayetteville Street for one of the biggest food-truck gatherings in the region. Arrive after 2 and the first lunch rush has thinned.

evening.title: Summer Concert Series: Carpe Diem Saxophone Quartet
evening.location: Fred Fletcher Park, 805 Washington St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The final Sunday of Raleigh Parks' summer series. Bring a blanket or a chair, and bring your own food and drink — Fletcher Park has no cafe, unlike Pullen.

evening.title: The Well x MOON DESTROYS (optional late add)
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, 224 S Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: A desert-rock double bill downtown if you want a second half to the evening. Doors at 7.

food.vegan_dish: The self-guided factory tour is free and several of the bars are dairy-free — check the labels at the counter
food.vegetarian_dish: Coffee and a bar; the whole factory floor is visible from the cafe
food.notes: 327 W Davie St, Suite 100. Open 10 AM Sunday. A guided tour is $25 if you want the full version.

food.vegan_dish: With this many trucks there are normally two or three fully plant-based kitchens — walk the whole street before you queue
food.vegetarian_dish: Arepas, tacos, pizza, noodles and shaved ice all reliably present
food.notes: This is the meal of the day. Split plates across trucks rather than committing to one line.

food.vegan_dish: Bring it with you — Fletcher has no vendors. Fiction Kitchen (428 S Dawson St) is fully vegetarian with a large vegan menu and is on the way
food.vegetarian_dish: Anything from Fiction Kitchen, or leftovers from the rodeo
food.notes: The concert explicitly asks you to bring your own food and drink at Fletcher Park. Fiction Kitchen takes reservations and fills up on Sundays.

alternatives.leg: Food Truck Rodeo (12–6 PM, on closed pavement)
alternatives.good_weather: Mostly sunny — this is the day for it. Fayetteville Street has some building shade on the west side after 3.
alternatives.rain: No storms in Sunday's forecast, but 90°F on asphalt is its own problem. The Museum of Natural Sciences and the Museum of History are both free and both a two-minute walk north up Fayetteville Street.

alternatives.leg: Summer Concert Series (6 PM, Fletcher Park lawn)
alternatives.good_weather: Get there by 5:30 for a shaded spot near the tree line.
alternatives.rain: The series cancels for weather rather than moving indoors. The Fourth Ward Gospel Extravaganza at the Fletcher Opera Theater is free at 4 PM, and Theatre Raleigh's Open Mic Night is free at 7.

practical_notes: 90°F and mostly sunny — the hottest sustained exposure of the week is standing on Fayetteville Street at midday. Come after 2 if you can.
Fayetteville Street parking decks are free on Sundays in Raleigh; the Wilmington and Salisbury Street decks are both a block off the rodeo.
Fletcher Park has no food vendors. This is the one leg where you must pack in.
Tips are encouraged at the concert — bring small bills.
The Dix Park trolley leaves from the Stone Houses Visitor Center, not the Gipson Play Plaza lot; they're on opposite ends of the park.

itineraries.title: Market, Dome and Giant Puppets — Chapel Hill and Carrboro
itineraries.theme: A producer-only market at 7 AM, a fulldome show in the afternoon, and Paperhand's giant puppets in the Forest Theatre after dark
itineraries.drive_time: About 15 minutes of driving. Carrboro to Franklin Street is 5 minutes; Morehead to the Forest Theatre is a 10-minute walk or a 3-minute drive.

weather.summary: Chance of rain showers and thunderstorms

itineraries.cost_range: $20–$60 per person. The market and the book sale are free to enter; the planetarium and Paperhand are the ticketed pieces.
itineraries.overview: Paperhand Puppet Project's 26th summer show is the anchor — giant puppets, masks, stilts and shadow work with a live band, in the stone amphitheatre off Country Club Road. Build the day backward from a 7 PM curtain: the Carrboro market at dawn, the library book sale mid-morning, and Morehead's dome through the hot part of the afternoon.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers' Market
morning.notes: One of the oldest producer-only markets in the state. Main-season Saturdays run 7 to noon and the good produce goes in the first ninety minutes.

morning.title: Friends Big Book Sale
morning.location: Chapel Hill Public Library, 100 Library Dr, Chapel Hill
morning.notes: The Friends' twice-yearly sale, open to everyone on Saturday. Sunday is the $10-a-bag day if you'd rather come back for volume.

afternoon.title: We Are Stars
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Forty-five minutes of air conditioning and a dome. Morehead runs five shows today; The Sun: Our Living Star is at noon and From Earth to the Universe at 3 if the timing suits better.

afternoon.title: From Earth to the Universe (second show, optional)
afternoon.location: Morehead Planetarium and Science Center, 250 E Franklin St, Chapel Hill
afternoon.notes: Stacking two shows is the cheapest way to spend the hottest two hours of a Chapel Hill Saturday indoors.

evening.title: Paperhand Puppet Project: The Wild Wisdom of the World
evening.location: Forest Theatre, 174 Country Club Rd, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Openers go on at 6:20, Paperhand at 7. Lawn, beach and camping chairs are NOT permitted — bring a cushion or a blanket and expect stone seating.

food.vegan_dish: Several bakers keep vegan pastries and there is usually a plant-based prepared-food stall — ask, the roster shifts seasonally
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastries, eggs, cheeses and breads straight from the growers
food.notes: Eating at the market is the point. Weaver Street Market is next door if you want a sit-down and a coffee.

food.vegan_dish: The kitchen keeps a substantial vegan section and will flag which curries are dairy-free — ask when you order
food.vegetarian_dish: Vegetable thali or a paneer dish
food.notes: 431 W Franklin St, in Courtyard. Five minutes from Morehead and it handles dietary requests better than most kitchens on Franklin.

food.place: Al's Burger Shack or a packed picnic
food.vegan_dish: Al's does a plant-based patty; otherwise pack a picnic from the morning market — plenty of the Forest Theatre crowd eats on the hill before curtain
food.vegetarian_dish: Veggie burger or a grilled cheese
food.notes: Eat by 6 and walk in for the 6:20 openers. Parking near Forest Theatre is limited, so arriving early is the real constraint, not the food.

alternatives.leg: Carrboro Farmers' Market (7 AM–noon, open-air shed)
alternatives.rain: The market runs under the shed rain or shine. Weaver Street's indoor cafe is thirty seconds away.

alternatives.leg: Paperhand at the Forest Theatre (7 PM, fully outdoors, stone seating)
alternatives.good_weather: Perfect — the amphitheatre is under trees and cools quickly after sunset.
alternatives.rain: Scattered storms are in Saturday's forecast and this show has no roof. Tickets are non-refundable but can be swapped to another night, and the run continues Fridays through Sundays until September 27. Local 506 has Machinegun Earl at 8 PM as a same-night indoor fallback.

practical_notes: No lawn, beach or camping chairs at the Forest Theatre — this catches people out every year. Bring a cushion.
Tickets for Paperhand are non-refundable but swappable to another date; children 3 and under are free and don't need a ticket.
Morehead's shows sell by session; check the ticket page before you drive over, since Saturday sessions can fill.
87°F with a chance of storms. The middle of this day is deliberately indoors.
The Forest Theatre is off Country Club Road with very little parking. Park on campus or downtown and walk the last stretch.

itineraries.title: Free Museum, $5 Beer, Ball Game — Durham
itineraries.theme: A Thursday built on the three cheapest good things in Durham: Community Day at the science museum, Mystery Beer at the Jug, and Triple-A baseball
itineraries.drive_time: About 40 minutes of driving. The museum is north of downtown, the Beer Lab is 20 minutes south in RTP, and the ballpark is back downtown — the one leg with real mileage.
itineraries.cost_range: $5–$45 per person. Free at the museum if you're a Durham County resident, $5 for the beer, $13+ for a Bulls ticket.
itineraries.overview: Durham County residents get into the Museum of Life and Science free all day with proof of address — butterfly house, train and Dinosaur Trail included. After that it's a Thursday: $5 bartender's-choice beer in RTP, then the Bulls hosting Norfolk at 6:45. If you'd rather trade the beer leg for art, the Nasher runs a free Women and Art gallery tour at 6.

morning.title: Durham Community Day
morning.location: Museum of Life and Science, 433 W Murray Ave, Durham
morning.price: Free for Durham County residents with proof of address; otherwise $24 adults
morning.notes: Bring a driver's license or a utility bill. The Magic Wings butterfly house and the Dinosaur Trail are the two things to prioritize if you only have half a day.

afternoon.title: Mystery Beer Thursdays
afternoon.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab, 5410 NC-55 Suite AH, Durham
afternoon.notes: Bartender's choice for $5, all day. Twenty minutes south of the museum, and the beer garden has shade.

evening.title: Gallery Guide Tour: Women and Art (alternative to the game)
evening.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
evening.notes: Marking Women's Equality Day. Free, one hour, and the museum's own admission is free — but it overlaps first pitch, so pick one.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Norfolk Tides
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: Third game of a six-game homestand. The outfield grass berm is the cheapest seat and catches whatever breeze there is.

food.vegan_dish: Ask which donuts are made without dairy that morning — the fried-chicken biscuits are not the play here
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit or the fried-green-tomato biscuit
food.notes: Quick, cheap and on the way north to the museum.

food.place: Museum of Life and Science cafe or a packed lunch
food.vegan_dish: The cafe's options are thin — pack a lunch and use the picnic tables outside the Dinosaur Trail
food.vegetarian_dish: Sandwiches and pizza at the cafe
food.notes: Community Day crowds the cafe. Packing in is faster and the outdoor tables are shaded.

food.vegan_dish: The stall lineup rotates; at least one counter usually plates a fully plant-based bowl — ask each vendor
food.vegetarian_dish: Pizza or a vegetable plate from whichever kitchen is open
food.notes: 530 Foster St, seven minutes' walk from the ballpark. Eat at 5:30 and stroll over for first pitch.

alternatives.leg: Durham Community Day (10 AM–5 PM, half outdoors)
alternatives.good_weather: Do the Dinosaur Trail and Hideaway Woods first, then the indoor galleries when the sun is highest.
alternatives.rain: The museum has substantial indoor space — the butterfly house, Investigate Health and the train depot all work in rain.
Rain delays at the DBAP are common in August and the concourse is partially covered. The Carolina Theatre and the Nasher tour are both indoor alternatives within ten minutes.

practical_notes: The NWS gridpoint forecast for Raleigh doesn't reach August 27 yet — check the forecast the morning of, especially for the ballgame.
Community Day is free only for Durham County residents and only with proof of address. Everyone else pays the regular $24 adult admission.
The Glass Jug's RTP location and its downtown location are different addresses running different events — Mystery Beer Thursdays is the RTP one.
The Nasher tour and first pitch overlap. Doing both is not possible; the Nasher tour is the better call if the weather is bad.
Bulls parking decks fill from 6:15. Church Street deck is a five-minute walk and usually still open.
